title: Power Automate: direct triggers for desktop flows
summary: The briefing accurately separates the planned direct-trigger capability from today's documented desktop-flow behaviour. Its dates match the roadmap, its data-policy controls are documented, and its licensing discussion preserves the general unattended-run and pay-as-you-go rules without inventing feature-specific requirements.

claims.claim: Data policy is at Power Platform admin center > Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy.
claims.quote: Select Security in the navigation pane. ... In the Security pane, under Settings, select Data and privacy. ... In the Data protection and privacy screen, select the Data policy section.

claims.claim: New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy creates a data policy using Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell.
claims.quote: Module: Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell Module. ... New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy ... Creates a new policy with the $NewPolicy object.

claims.where: controls[1].governs and note; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: Data policies govern desktop flow modules in the environments covered by the policy.
claims.quote: Power Automate allows you to create and enforce DLP policies that classify desktop flow modules and individual module actions as Business, Non-business, or Blocked.

claims.claim: A data policy can manage both desktop flow modules and cloud flow connectors.
claims.quote: You can define a DLP policy that manages both desktop flow modules and cloud flow connectors.

claims.claim: The desktop flow connector can be governed in data policies like other connectors.
claims.quote: Ability to govern desktop flow orchestration: The desktop flow connector can be governed in your policies like any other connector in all environments.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented how direct triggers themselves are governed or whether connector policies govern their new triggering route.
claims.quote: Searched: "desktop flows" "direct triggers" licensing default data policies limits. Opened Data loss prevention (DLP) policy creation and Manage data policies; module and connector governance is documented, but no direct-trigger mechanism or connector association is stated.

claims.claim: Adding desktop flow modules to data policies causes noncompliant desktop flows to be evaluated and suspended.
claims.quote: When desktop flow modules are added to DLP policies, your tenant's desktop flows are evaluated against them, and they're suspended if they're noncompliant.

claims.claim: The documented tenant-level data-policy steps require the Power Platform Administrator role.
claims.quote: To follow the steps described in this article for tenant-level policies, sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator role.

claims.claim: Environment-level data-policy steps require Environment Admin permissions outside the Dataverse-database case.
claims.quote: To follow the steps for environment-level policies, you need to have Power Apps Environment Admin permissions.

claims.claim: Environment-level data-policy steps require System Administrator instead when the environment has a Dataverse database.
claims.quote: For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.
